[LCCO.3.7] **The correlation counter.** Each engine holds one counter, which is
0 when the engine is created. Taking a value yields `g<k>`, with `k` the
counter's value in decimal, and advances the counter by one. The engine must
take values at these points only, and in this order:

1. When a rule fires, before any of its actions runs: one value for each `call`
   in its RHS that has no `as` or a computed `as` ([LRST.1.2]), in source order;
   then one for each `after` clause with no `as` whose body reads a binding of
   the rule ([LTAC.3.5], [LTAC.3.6]), in source order.
2. When a synthesized terminal fires — an `after` follow-up or a continuation
   sibling ([RLOW.14.7]) — before any of its actions runs: one value for each
   `call` in its own body that has no `as` or a computed `as`, in source order.
   A `call` with a continuation in that body takes none: it carries a literal
   `as`, or the compiler refuses it ([LCCO.3.8]).

**A value is taken whether or not it is used.** A computed `as` that evaluates
to a non-empty key still takes one. A call that its `cooldown` gate holds back
([RLOW.4.6.6.1]), or that a NaN argument refuses ([RLOW.7.3.1]), still takes
one, because the value is taken before the gate decides and before the
arguments are evaluated.

The counter is engine state and is not recorded. A replay re-derives it, taking
the same values in the same order from the same inputs ([LDET.2.2]).
